question: The NHRC Guidelines (1997) for custodial deaths specify that the post-mortem must be conducted by a board of at least how many doctors, with video recording mandatory?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. A single doctor is insufficient for a custodial autopsy under NHRC guidelines.

answers.text: A board of at least two doctors, with video recording of the entire procedure

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The NHRC 1997 guidelines mandate a minimum two-doctor board and mandatory video recording of the entire post-mortem procedure for custodial deaths.

answers.text: A board of three doctors including a civil surgeon, with photographs only

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The mandatory minimum is two doctors; video recording (not photographs alone) is required.

answers.text: A board of five forensic specialists with a magistrate present

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Five specialists are not specified; the requirement is at minimum two doctors. Magistrate presence is for the inquest, not necessarily the autopsy.

overallFeedback.feedback: Memorise: NHRC 1997 custodial death PM = at least 2 doctors + video recording of the entire procedure. Photographs alone are insufficient.
Correct. NHRC 1997 custodial death guidelines: minimum two-doctor board + mandatory video recording of the entire PM. This is frequently tested.
